entities.summary:
Berengar Fredol or Bérenger Frédol was a French canon lawyer and Cardinal-Bishop of Frascati.
He played a significant role in shaping the Catholic Church's legal and administrative structures during the late Middle Ages.
Born in 1250 in France, Fredol rose to prominence through his education at the University of Paris and his appointment as a canon at the Notre-Dame Cathedral.

As a key figure in the Curia Romana, Fredol contributed to the development of the Canon Law, a collection of ecclesiastical laws that governed the Church's internal affairs.
He also participated in several synods and councils, including the Council of Vienne, where he played a crucial role in resolving theological disputes.

Fredol's legacy extends beyond his contributions to the Canon Law, as he also helped establish the office of the Cardinal-Bishop of Frascati, a position that would become increasingly powerful during the Renaissance.
This institution became a hub for papal politics and a center of influence for the Catholic Church in Italy.

The legacy of Berengar Fredol can be seen in the continued relevance of the Canon Law, which remains an important part of Catholic canon.
The modern Catholic Church still uses many of the principles established by Fredol during his time as Cardinal-Bishop of Frascati.
